    emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    dept VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    salary NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL,

    emp_id INT REFERENCES employees(emp_id),

# 📊 SQL Architecture, Window Functions & Query Tuning Track

Welcome to the **SQL Architecture, Window Functions & Query Tuning Track** materialized by **Trak**.

This workspace is an in-depth curriculum covering logical query processing order, window functions (`ROW_NUMBER`, `DENSE_RANK`, `LEAD`, `LAG`), recursive CTEs for hierarchical tree traversal, indexing strategies, and query plan optimization.

## 📚 Syllabus & Module Map

| Module | Title | Key Topics & Internals |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-relational-model` | Relational Algebra & ACID | Relational model, Codd's rules, ACID guarantees, DDL/DML/DCL/TCL boundaries |
| `01-basic-queries-select-where-group` | Logical Query Processing | Logical execution order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY |
| `02-joins-deep-dive-inner-left-cross` | Joins Deep Dive | INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER, CROSS, Anti-Joins, Non-Equi Joins |
| `03-aggregate-functions-and-grouping-sets` | Aggregates & Grouping Sets | `SUM`, `AVG`, `COUNT(*)`, `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP`, `CUBE` multidimensional grouping |
| `04-subqueries-correlated-vs-uncorrelated` | Subqueries & Correlated Subqueries | Scalar subqueries, correlated subqueries, `EXISTS` vs `IN`, `ALL` vs `ANY` |
| `05-common-table-expressions-ctes` | CTEs & Recursive Hierarchies | `WITH ... AS`, Recursive CTEs (`WITH RECURSIVE`) for organizational tree traversal |
| `06-window-functions-ranking-and-numbering` | Window Functions (Ranking) | `ROW_NUMBER()`, `RANK()`, `DENSE_RANK()`, `NTILE()`, `PARTITION BY`, `ORDER BY` |
| `07-window-functions-lead-lag-and-frames` | Window Offsets & Framing | `LEAD()`, `LAG()`, `FIRST_VALUE()`, `ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING` |
| `08-set-operations-union-intersect-except` | Set Operations | `UNION` (deduplicating sort) vs `UNION ALL` (zero overhead), `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT` |
| `09-conditional-expressions-case-coalesce` | Logic & Three-Valued Logic | `CASE WHEN`, `COALESCE()`, `NULLIF()`, Three-Valued Logic (`TRUE`, `FALSE`, `UNKNOWN`) |
| `10-data-manipulation-upsert-and-merge` | Upserts & Returning | `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (Upsert), `MERGE INTO`, `RETURNING` clauses |
| `11-database-views-and-materialized-views` | Views & Materialized Views | Standard Views vs Materialized Views, `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` |
| `12-indexes-and-b-tree-query-acceleration` | Index Mechanics | Composite index leading column rule, covering indexes (`INCLUDE`), cardinality |
| `13-query-planning-and-cost-optimization` | Query Cost & Optimization | Cost-based optimizer (CBO), predicate pushdown, join order selection |
| `14-schema-design-and-normalization` | Schema Normalization | 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, Surrogate vs Natural Keys (UUID v7, BIGINT), Foreign Keys |
| `15-transactions-and-isolation-levels` | Transaction Isolation Levels | Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable, Phantom reads |
| `16-temporal-and-time-series-queries` | Time-Series & Moving Averages | `generate_series`, date truncation (`date_trunc`), 7-day rolling moving averages |
| `17-analytics-and-pivoting` | Pivoting & Analytical Reports | `FILTER (WHERE ...)`, crosstab matrix pivoting, conditional aggregations |
| `18-interview-questions-and-drills` | Interview Mastery Drills | Top 10 SQL gotchas (NULL comparisons, COUNT(col) vs COUNT(*), Cartesian products) |

---

## 🛠️ How to Practice
Each module contains:
- `README.md` — Deep theoretical explanation and architecture notes.
- `example.sql` — Fully runnable concept demonstration.
- `exercise/starter.sql` — Hands-on problem with `TODO` markers.
- `exercise/solution.sql` — Complete reference solution.

## 🎯 Recursive CTE Structure
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy_tree AS (
    -- Anchor Member
    SELECT id, name, manager_id, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- Recursive Member
    SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, h.level + 1 
    FROM employees e 
    JOIN hierarchy_tree h ON e.manager_id = h.id
)
SELECT * FROM hierarchy_tree;
```

-- 05: Organizational Tree Traversal with Recursive CTE
WITH RECURSIVE OrgChart AS (
    SELECT emp_id, name, manager_id, 1 AS depth
    FROM employees
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.emp_id, e.name, e.manager_id, o.depth + 1
    FROM employees e
    JOIN OrgChart o ON e.manager_id = o.emp_id
)
SELECT * FROM OrgChart ORDER BY depth, emp_id;

**Technical Internals & Architectural Notes:**

## 🎯 Difference Between Ranking Functions
- `ROW_NUMBER()`: Always sequential integers (`1, 2, 3, 4`).
- `RANK()`: Ties share rank; next rank skips numbers (`1, 2, 2, 4`).
- `DENSE_RANK()`: Ties share rank; next rank does NOT skip (`1, 2, 2, 3`).

## ⏱️ When to use & When NOT to use

SELECT 
    emp_id, name, dept, salary,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS row_num,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank_num
FROM employees;

## 🎯 Leading Column Rule
An index on `(dept, salary)` accelerates:
- `WHERE dept = 'Engineering'` (Uses leading column)
- `WHERE dept = 'Engineering' AND salary > 90000` (Uses both)
- **DOES NOT accelerate** `WHERE salary > 90000` (Leading column omitted!).
